node.label: Gail Bederman
node.date_label: “The Women Have Had Charge of the Church Work Long Enough” (1989) · “‘Civilization,’ the Decline of Middle-Class Manliness…” (1992) · Manliness and Civilization: original publication (1995)
node.description: A historian of gender and race in the United States. Manliness and Civilization asks how changing ideals of manhood could reinforce white authority while also being contested. Its selected chapter opening distinguishes the projects of Wells, Hall, Gilman and Roosevelt rather than making them one coordinated movement. Anne-Marie Harvey’s substantive discussion identifies Bederman’s account of a shift from self-restraint toward celebrated masculine force; that account is retained as an interpretation with a later reader’s qualifications, not a universal sequence.
node.representative_figures_and_works: “The Women Have Had Charge of the Church Work Long Enough” (1989); “‘Civilization,’ the Decline of Middle-Class Manliness, and Ida B. Wells’s Antilynching Campaign (1892–94)” (1992); Manliness and Civilization (1995; 1996 paperback distinct).
node.scope_note: New identity is the Notre Dame historian and sole author of the selected writings. Both early articles and full monograph unread. Argument evidence is limited to the indexed primary passage and Harvey’s explicitly attributed discussion; direct scan access failed. The primary extract preserves differences among the historical actors. No claim of a uniform white masculinity or a direct intellectual influence on later scholars.

verification.note: Only the indexed primary passage around printed pp. 42–43 read, on distinct uses of civilization in four cases. Direct PDF retrieval returned 403 in both local and web access; no complete PDF or chapter reading claimed. The extract is bounded evidence supplemented by the separately read named substantive reader, not a publisher description or whole-book certification. Addendum 2026-10-25: After the frozen 1.171 indexed/mediated check, the same public scan was successfully retrieved via its S3 CDN: https://s3.amazonaws.com/files.commons.gc.cuny.edu/wp-content/blogs.dir/4188/files/2018/08/Bederman-Manliness-and-Civilization.pdf . Printed pp. 4–9 and 42–43 were then read through page OCR; PDF page 3 (printed 2–3) visually inspected to confirm the two-page scan mapping. Pp. 5–8 define manhood as a historical process relating bodies, identities and authority; pp. 42–43 explain racial/civilizational strategies. P. 43 explicitly limits the selected cases to varied discursive positions rather than representativeness or measured effects on others. Full chapter/book and endnotes remain unread; historical examples are not independently checked. Earlier 403 and indexed/Harvey reading limits remain the historical scope of the earlier check; no claim or edge changes follow.
